indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the word for a rover is read backwards

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer, a nomad

explanation.surface: Another wandering man heads back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NOMAD round. Damon, of Damon and Pythias, is the classical model of a loyal friend or companion, and it is also simply a man's name, hence 'Fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon is a man's name, and a fellow is a man or chap; Damon of legend was also a devoted companion.

clue.text: Doing away with the work of a chemist

explanation.surface: Someone abolishing the pharmacist's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense with something is to do without it; a pharmacist dispenses medicines, making up prescriptions as their trade.

indicators.note: one word is placed in the course of another, sitting inside it

parts.note: sorcery is magic
net is a mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A charming cloth woven into a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' reads as praise for the fabric but is the definition, in the sense of drawing iron. 'included during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet attracts, so something magnetic is drawing or alluring.

clue.text: Something to be specially observed from new books with hesitation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the crossword's usual books
and means with, joining things
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A note worth heeding drawn from fresh volumes, read haltingly.
explanation.walkthrough: A Latin word, literally 'thing to be noted'. 'from' simply links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin gerundive meaning a thing that must be noted, so a memorandum of something important to heed.

explanation.surface: Senior figures who might play trumpet in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for senior officers or bosses; read literally it suggests the leading brass players of a band.

parts.note: togs are clothes, so one garment in the singular is a tog

explanation.surface: One item of clothing in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes are informally 'togs'; 'Singular' asks for the one-item form TOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose woollen wrap worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, and a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: A family member at the pub keeps banging a spinning drum.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the nearby pub. The definition fits the rotating cylinder of a revolver or a winch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating cylinder of a revolver or a capstan is called by this name, as is a cask.

clue.text: Gold to become red perhaps, dark coppery-red

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
skin that burns in the sun turns red, one way of reddening

explanation.surface: Gilded hair reddening into a deep copper shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour word, mostly for hair, describing a reddish-brown shade.

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for complaining is taken as it sounds

parts.note: to sigh is to voice discontent with a long breath

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles out loud about the regulation dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimensions given in a standard scale, like a shoe or dress measure.

clue.text: When something rare is seen — hearing where one should put it

indicators.note: hearing tells us to take the word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: the site or placement of something is its siting

explanation.surface: A rare creature has been spotted, and there is debate over its proper place.
explanation.walkthrough: SITING and SIGHTING sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting something unusual, such as a rare bird, is an observation of it.

indicators.note: rearranged means the remaining letters are put in a new order
without means a letter is left out of the word recapture

parts.note: the setter takes castle as C, which is not a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A gap appears when a seized fortress is reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes C from RECAPTURE and 'rearranged' shuffles the rest. Castle as C is the setter's slip: the usual castle letter, R, cannot be removed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or gap, as in the adjustable opening of a camera lens.

clue.text: Salesman brought up chemical compound for bleach

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word climbs the column, read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an oxide is a compound of oxygen with another element

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman produces a bleaching agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses REP to give PER. 'for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen peroxide is the chemical used to lighten hair, hence peroxide blonde.

parts.note: not an angry woman but the queen whose funeral route is marked by a series of English memorial crosses

explanation.surface: An angry woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward I set up stone crosses where his queen's body rested on its way to London; Charing Cross is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, borne by the medieval queen commemorated by the crosses.

clue.text: Man on hill taken in by interminable full-toned speech

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed by the following word
interminable means with no end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a rich voice is full-toned
he stands for a man
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man on a hill delivers a booming, endless oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full-toned' describes a voice; cut short by 'interminable', it opens to hold the man and hill, which 'taken in by' signals. 'on' just stacks one piece above the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory or persuasive language, often grandiose, is this art of speaking.

clue.text: Not easy on vessel for one who is uncompromising

parts.note: something not easy is hard
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A tough life aboard a ship for someone who won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'for' are link words here.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes an unyielding, inflexible position, especially in politics.

parts.note: the chief figure of a gang or ring, read as the head of a round group

explanation.surface: Who comes first in a circle?
explanation.walkthrough: A circle has no first place, which is the joke; a ring is also a criminal gang, and its chief instigator is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The instigator who heads a gang or a group causing trouble.

parts.note: a refund of tax read as coming back through the annual form filed with the revenue

explanation.surface: Money back?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: the form filed with the tax authorities is called a return, and a rebate is money returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money handed back, and this form is how one claims back overpaid tax.

indicators.note: unravelling tangled thread breaks its order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untangling something is regarded as simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unravelling' rearranges IS SEEN AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being effortless or uncomplicated is simplicity.

clue.text: Head off from town likely to give way

indicators.note: the head of the word is cut off, removing its first letter

parts.note: Dunstable is a market town in Bedfordshire, England

explanation.surface: Leaving town is a shaky proposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off from' removes the D from DUNSTABLE, a town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsteady or insecure may collapse or fall.

clue.text: Plant of outstanding excellence in front of little Roderick

indicators.note: in front of places one piece before the other in the answer

parts.note: golden describes something superb, as in a golden age
Rod is the short form of the name Roderick

explanation.surface: Roderick puts on a top-class display of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall perennial with yellow flower spikes, a garden and wild flower.

clue.text: Ice left at end of sweet drink

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Ice left at end of sweet drink' for LIQUOR: no parse builds LIQUOR from these words (L for left plus a piece for 'Ice' does not give IQUOR), and a search finds no other wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Ice left at end of sweet drink

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Shared out fairly for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges EVENLY; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A given name borne mostly by women, so it stands for a woman.

parts.note: not a woman named Pauline but St Paul's letters in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A woman called Pauline puts pen to paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pauline' looks like a woman's name but means of St Paul, whose New Testament letters bear this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter, especially one of the apostles' letters in the Bible.

clue.text: Not study importance leading to succession

indicators.note: not means the word for study is left out of the longer word

parts.note: a matter of consequence is one of importance
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Skipping revision matters, and leads to a chain of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes CON from CONSEQUENCE; 'leading to' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of things following one after another in order.

clue.text: Soon with impetus make, initially, progress in water

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Push hard early on and you will make headway through the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S, W, I and M from the first four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving through water by strokes of the arms and legs.

indicators.note: included means the run of letters sits within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tongue thrown in the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversely' suggests reversal but is the word holding the letters, read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic tongue of Ireland or Scotland goes by this old name.

clue.text: But it is not where banker sleeps

definitions.text: But it is not where banker sleeps

parts.words: But it is not where banker sleeps
parts.note: a banker is a river, which has banks, and its bed is no place to sleep

explanation.surface: A financier's bed? Not this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The channel floor over which a river flows.

indicators.note: smeared means spread messily about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Irene has smeared gum all over the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smeared' rearranges GUM IRENE; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A light baked confection of whisked egg white and sugar, served as a small cake.

clue.text: Bridge partners always show cynical contempt

parts.note: in bridge South and North play as partners
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Card players permanently scornful of others.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, North with South and East with West.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl the lip and speak scornfully is to mock with disdain.
